CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER Accused in Special Case No.28/2024 pending before the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, Tumakuru, arising out of Crime No.154/2023 registered by Kodigenahalli Police Station, Tumkuru, for the offences punishable under Sections 376(I) and 376(L) of IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
2.

entities.text: Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-1, Tumakuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.

3. F.I.R. in Crime No.154/2023 was registered in Kodigenahalli Police Station, Tumkuru, against the petitioner herein initially for the offences punishable under Section 376(L) of IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, NC: 2024:KHC:32736 based on the first information received from the mother of the victim girl on 21.12.2023.
During the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested and remanded to the judicial custody on 22.12.2023.
The investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
The bail application filed by the petitioner before the trial Court in Crl.Mis.No.40/2024 was rejected on 19.02.2024 and therefore, he is before this court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he is aged about 48 years.
The victim and the first informant who is her mother have been already examined before the trial Court and they have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP who has seriously opposed the bail application submits that victim is a minor girl and she is mentally retarded.
Petitioner has committed a heinous offence and accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
Learned Counsel for respondent No.2 has also supported the arguments of the learned HCGP.

Krishnappa vs State Of Karnataka on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138069126/
2 7.

The material on record goes to show that respondent No.2 who is the mother of the victim girl has approached the police on 21.12.2023 alleging that on 10.12.2023, the petitioner herein had taken her minor daughter along with him and had sexually assaulted her in his bathroom.
According to the first informant on the date of incident itself, the victim girl had informed her about the incident.
But there is a delay of more than 10 days in lodging the FIR.
The victim girl and first informant have been examined before the trial Court as P.Ws.1 & 2.
Perusal of their deposition would go to show that they have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Petitioner is aged about 48 years and he is in custody from 22.12.2023.
He has no criminal antecedents.
The trial court while rejecting petitioner's bail application has observed that petitioner is at liberty to file a fresh petition after evidence of P.W.1.
Considering the aforesaid aspects NC: 2024:KHC:32736 of the matter, I am of the opinion that petitioner's request for grant of regular bail is required to be answered in the affirmative.

8. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
